MISSION CONTROL — PHASE 2 / SYS-004
ADD VALIDATION GATE FIRST

You are operating inside Mission Control.

Role:
Act as Van / senior systems engineer.

Objective:
Implement the first Phase 2 upgrade:
SYS-004 — Add deterministic task result validation gate.

Current system:
- Local LLM runtime: Ollama
- Models available:
  - mistral:7b
  - qwen2.5-coder:14b
  - deepseek-coder:6.7b
- Queue files:
  - queue/pending.json
  - queue/active.json
  - queue/completed.json
  - queue/blocked.json
- Runner:
  - queue-runner.sh
- Logs:
  - logs/system.log

Non-negotiable rules:
- Script controls task state, not the model.
- Model output is advisory only.
- No silent failures.
- Logs must reflect real execution.
- Keep it simple.
- Use bash/python primitives only.
- Do not introduce frameworks.
- Do not overengineer.

Task:
Create a deterministic validator:

scripts/validate_task_result.py

Validator requirements:
1. Accept input as a JSON file path argument.
2. Validate that the file exists.
3. Validate that contents are valid JSON.
4. Validate required top-level fields:
   - id
   - status
   - result
5. Validate status is one of:
   - completed
   - blocked
   - failed
6. Validate result is not empty.
7. Print clear validation messages.
8. Exit with deterministic exit codes.

Exit codes:
- 0 = valid
- 1 = file missing
- 2 = invalid json
- 3 = missing required field
- 4 = invalid status
- 5 = empty result
- 9 = unexpected validator error

Also create test fixtures:

tests/fixtures/valid_result.json
tests/fixtures/invalid_json.json
tests/fixtures/missing_result.json
tests/fixtures/invalid_status.json
tests/fixtures/empty_result.json

Then test the validator manually with:

python3 scripts/validate_task_result.py tests/fixtures/valid_result.json
python3 scripts/validate_task_result.py tests/fixtures/invalid_json.json
python3 scripts/validate_task_result.py tests/fixtures/missing_result.json
python3 scripts/validate_task_result.py tests/fixtures/invalid_status.json
python3 scripts/validate_task_result.py tests/fixtures/empty_result.json

Expected:
- valid_result.json exits 0
- invalid_json.json exits 2
- missing_result.json exits 3
- invalid_status.json exits 4
- empty_result.json exits 5

Important:
Do not modify queue-runner.sh yet unless absolutely necessary.
This task is only to add and prove the validator.

After completion, report:
- files created
- test commands run
- exit codes observed
- any issues found
- recommended next patch

queued.task: MISSION CONTROL — SINGLE OUTPUT ENFORCEMENT LOCK v1  ──────────────────────────────────────── PROBLEM ────────────────────────────────────────  Multiple system modules are bypassing the final response gate and writing directly to the UI layer.  This causes: - system messages appearing in chat - debug logs leaking into UI - contract/validation blocks showing - inconsistent assistant output  ──────────────────────────────────────── ROOT CAUSE ────────────────────────────────────────  There are still DIRECT UI writes occurring outside:  finalizeChatResponse()  Specifically: - system fallback handlers - execution engine logs - validation pipeline outputs - router-level early returns  ──────────────────────────────────────── MANDATORY FIX: CENTRALIZE ALL OUTPUTS  RULE:  ❗ NO MODULE MAY WRITE TO UI DIRECTLY  ONLY ONE ALLOWED PATH EXISTS:  ALL OUTPUTS → finalizeChatResponse() → UI  ──────────────────────────────────────── STEP 1 — HARD BLOCK DIRECT UI CALLS  Search and REMOVE ALL:  res.json({ reply: ... }) res.send(...) appendMessage(...) pushToUI(...) emitResponse(...) return response from system handlers  IF IT DOES NOT GO THROUGH finalizeChatResponse(): → IT IS INVALID  ──────────────────────────────────────── STEP 2 — ENFORCE OUTPUT PIPELINE  ALL SYSTEMS MUST DO:  output → internal_event_bus → finalizeChatResponse → UI  NOTHING ELSE  ──────────────────────────────────────── STEP 3 — SYSTEM MESSAGE HANDLING  System messages MUST:  ✔ be logged only ✔ stored in audit log ✔ never returned to chat layer  ──────────────────────────────────────── STEP 4 — FALLBACK RULE  If finalizeChatResponse receives system content:  → DROP IT → DO NOT DISPLAY → DO NOT SUBSTITUTE AS USER CONTENT  ONLY allow assistant-safe outputs  ──────────────────────────────────────── STEP 5 — SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH  UI layer MUST ONLY accept:  {   from: "Nettie",   text: "<clean assistant response>" }  NO EXCEPTIONS  ──────────────────────────────────────── SUCCESS CRITERIA  ✔ No system text in UI ever ✔ No contract/debug leaks ✔ No fallback messages visible ✔ Only Nettie appears to user ✔ Deterministic output pipeline ✔ Fully GPT-like interface achieved  ──────────────────────────────────────── WHY THIS IS THE FINAL FIX  This eliminates:  → parallel output paths → legacy system leaks → bypass rendering bugs  AND forces a single controlled UI pipeline

blocked.task: MISSION CONTROL COMMAND — BLOG CONTENT EXECUTION (SDL LAUNCH)  Objective: Execute the initial SDL blog content build using structured workflow, controlled ownership, and review-gated delivery.  ================================================== CHAIN OF COMMAND ================  Nettie (Coordinator) → validates inputs, enforces doctrine, assigns execution  Torina (Chief Media Officer) → owns content strategy execution + quality control  Scribe (Execution Agent) → produces final blog articles (MDX-ready)  Polish (Review Agent) → validates tone, clarity, and brand alignment before release  ================================================== TASK SET ========  Create the following initial blog articles:  1. Why Outdated Websites Cost Local Businesses Leads 2. Why We Rebuild WordPress Sites Instead of Maintaining Plugin Stacks 3. What a Modern Service Business Website Needs in 2026 4. Website Redesign Checklist for Contractors and Home Service Companies 5. When Does a Doctor’s Office Website Become a HIPAA Concern? 6. Why Fast Websites Build More Trust 7. When a Business Needs More Than a Website 8. Why Custom Digital Systems Beat Disconnected Tools  ================================================== EXECUTION FLOW ==============  STEP 1 — NETTIE  * Load SDL Blog Content Creation Prompt (source of truth) * Validate:    * positioning alignment   * target audience clarity   * article list completeness * Assign articles sequentially to Torina (ONE at a time) * Do NOT batch assign  STEP 2 — TORINA  * Translate article into execution brief:    * topic intent   * target reader   * business problem   * sales relevance   * internal linking targets * Pass structured brief to Scribe * Do NOT write article content  STEP 3 — SCRIBE  * Generate FULL MDX blog article with:    * filename   * frontmatter   * H1 title   * structured sections:      * intro     * problem     * why it matters     * signs     * better approach     * next steps   * internal links (3–5 max)   * compliant claims only   * bottom CTA  STRICT RULES:  * No fluff * No fake stats * No hype language * No SEO spam * Business-owner readable * Clean formatting only  STEP 4 — POLISH  * Review for:    * tone consistency   * clarity   * professionalism   * SDL positioning * Fix minor issues only * If major issues → return to Scribe  STEP 5 — TORINA FINAL APPROVAL  * Confirm:    * structure complete   * formatting clean   * CTA correct   * internal links correct  ================================================== DELIVERY REQUIREMENT (CRITICAL) ===============================  After EACH article is completed and approved:  Torina must trigger email delivery with:  Subject: SDL Blog Draft — [Article Title]  Body:  * Article title * Short 1–2 sentence summary * Notes (if any)  Attachment / Included Content:  * Full MDX article (clean copy-paste ready)  Send to:  * [Patrick@SentinelsDesignLab.com](mailto:Patrick@SentinelsDesignLab.com) * [SentinelsTechnologyGroup@gmail.com](mailto:SentinelsTechnologyGroup@gmail.com)  ================================================== GATING RULES ============  * NO next article begins until:    * current article is completed   * reviewed   * emailed  * ALL outputs must be:    * review-ready   * production-quality   * aligned with SDL doctrine  * NO agent may:    * skip steps   * self-assign new tasks   * bypass Nettie coordination blocked.task: MISSION CONTROL — FIX NETTIE/MC → HERMES RESPONSE CONNECTION  Current observed issue: Backend Hermes v2.1 validation passes, but Nettie/MC UI still responds only: “Nettie: Standing by.”  This suggests the UI/backend chat path is not receiving, forwarding, or rendering the real Hermes response after the Base44 cleanup.  Objective: Restore live Nettie/MC browser chat → backend /api/chat → Hermes → real Nettie response in UI.  Do NOT modify UI design. Do NOT rebuild the UI. Do NOT remove IRL gating. Do NOT remove Hermes routing. Do NOT change Hermes v2.1 decomposition behavior unless required to preserve response shape. Do NOT reintroduce fake execution. Do NOT create a separate AI/API key path.  Required investigation:  1. Verify frontend chat submit path:    - locate the Nettie chat send handler    - verify it POSTs to /api/chat    - verify request body includes the user message    - verify response parsing reads the actual backend reply text  2. Verify Vite proxy:    - confirm /api is proxied from localhost:5173 to localhost:4174    - confirm browser-side /api/chat reaches backend server  3. Verify backend /api/chat response shape:    - curl POST /api/chat directly    - inspect full JSON    - identify where real Hermes/Nettie text exists    - confirm UI expects the same field path  4. Fix response-shape mismatch if present:    - preserve existing backend fields    - add compatibility fields only if needed    - frontend should render:      data.reply.text      or the correct canonical response text field  5. Verify “Standing by” source:    - find exact string “Standing by”    - determine whether it is a fallback, static default, or failed-response handler    - replace fallback behavior only where incorrect    - keep valid offline/error fallback behavior  6. Validate live browser chat:    - send “Nettie, confirm live Hermes bridge.”    - UI must display a real routed response, not “Standing by”    - hard refresh must preserve chat history if that was already working  Validation commands: - node --check on modified JS/JSX files - npm run build if applicable - curl -s http://localhost:4174/api/health - curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4174/api/chat -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"message":"Nettie, confirm live Hermes bridge.","sender":"Patrick","channel":"mission-control"}' - browser UI live send test  Return ONLY:  - Nettie/MC → Hermes live response status: pass/fail - Root cause - Files modified - Files created - Standing by fallback source found: yes/no - /api/chat backend response valid: yes/no - frontend response parser fixed: yes/no - Vite proxy valid: yes/no - IRL gating preserved: yes/no - Hermes routing preserved: yes/no - Fake execution reintroduced: yes/no - UI design modified: yes/no - Health endpoint: pass/fail - Direct chat curl: pass/fail - Browser chat live response: pass/fail - Build/syntax command - Build/syntax exit code - Recommended next phase  Begin.

completedRecent.task: Nettie / Van — FIX operational brief classification at the source (not UI).  Observed failure: Jobs still appear in multiple sections: - RUNNING - ACTIVE / IN-PROGRESS - QUEUED  ACTIVE / IN-PROGRESS must not exist. Each job must appear in exactly ONE section.  Root cause: Operational brief generator is using overlapping filters instead of exclusive classification.  Required fix (must all be applied):  1. REMOVE ACTIVE / IN-PROGRESS section completely - delete from renderer - delete from any aggregation logic  2. Enforce strict exclusive classification BEFORE rendering:  For each job:  if (status === "running") → RUNNING else if (status === "queued") → QUEUED else if (status === "blocked" || providerOutage === true) → BLOCKED else if (status === "completed" || status === "cancelled") → COMPLETED else → ignore  3. Build sections using a SINGLE PASS:  const buckets = {   running: [],   queued: [],   blocked: [],   completed: [] }  for each job:   assign to ONE bucket only  4. Deduplicate BEFORE bucketing:  const seen = new Set()  for each job:   if seen.has(job.id) → skip   else → seen.add(job.id)  5. Counts must match unique jobs: running + queued + blocked + completed = total unique jobs  6. DO NOT reuse previous “active” arrays or merged lists  ---  ## Validation (must pass all)  A. No jobId appears in more than one section  B. ACTIVE / IN-PROGRESS does not exist  C. Counts reflect unique jobs only  D. Queued count remains accurate (Van load signal)  ---  ## Report  - classification logic location (file + function) - ACTIVE removal confirmed - before vs after counts - confirmation: no duplicates remain
